title: Register Clay preview handlers under Jupyter base_url
description: Why: Binder serves Jupyter under a per-user base path like /user/<session>/, but the Clay preview server handlers are currently registered as absolute paths. The frontend correctly requests base_url-prefixed routes, so Binder returns 404 for /clay-preview endpoints even though the extension is enabled and Clay itself runs.\n\nWhat: update server handler registration to join routes against Jupyter's configured base_url, then validate Binder-style prefixed routes resolve.

title: Pin BinderHub thin image to immutable GHCR digest
description: Why: .binder/Dockerfile still defaults to ghcr.io/sashakile/clojnder-binder:latest, so BinderHub builds remain nondeterministic even though CI publishes deterministic tags.\n\nWhat: replace the floating latest reference in .binder/Dockerfile with an immutable GHCR digest (with a comment noting the corresponding tag), and document the pinning behavior.

title: Fix deployed Binder extension compatibility and render route smoke coverage
description: Why: the deployed Binder build still fails at runtime with JupyterLab shared singleton version mismatches and a 404 on /clay-preview/render. This indicates the packaged labextension/runtime combination is not compatible in the published image, and current CI does not exercise the deployed JupyterLab frontend/backend integration path.\n\nWhat: diagnose the exact compatibility gap, align the packaged labextension with the runtime JupyterLab stack, and add validation that catches render-route regressions in the built Binder image.

title: Fix binder publish workflow sha tag mismatch
description: Why: the publish workflow now resolves a deterministic Binder base image reference, but it constructs the sha tag from the full 40-character GITHUB_SHA while docker/metadata-action publishes sha tags using the short 7-character form. Binder image publish therefore tries to pull a non-existent base image tag and CI fails.\n\nWhat: make the Binder publish step derive the same sha tag format as docker/metadata-action so downstream image references resolve correctly.

title: Use deterministic tags for published container images
description: Why: Docker/Binder deploys currently rely on floating latest tags, which makes deployments non-deterministic and prevents consumers from pinning to exact builds.\n\nWhat: update image publishing and downstream Dockerfiles/docs so published images also receive deterministic version tags (at minimum commit-based tags, and version/release tags when available), and downstream references can pin to them instead of latest only.

title: Optimize Docker images for lightweight Binder startup
description: Binder startup is slow due to a large Docker build context (198MB node_modules copied without .dockerignore) and an oversized base image (default-jdk instead of JRE). Fix: add .dockerignore, switch to default-jre-headless, remove unused apt packages, improve layer ordering in .binder/Dockerfile to maximize cache reuse.
